source_specific_acceptance_reasoning: The prior card correctly identified the central bounded contribution: a natural-language specification is transformed into a hybrid pseudo-program plus task-conditioned PEFT artifact for a frozen lightweight interpreter, and the paper reports substantial exact-match and local-runtime results. It nevertheless contains material factual and semantic errors that cannot receive an ACCEPT or NARROW verdict. FuzzyBench-10M is described as synthetic and released, not proprietary; the currently public verified dataset is only a 50,678-example test/test_clean subset, so the precise boundary is incomplete public release of the claimed 10M corpus. The paper does not define probabilistic semantics or state that correctness is probabilistic. Its empirical exact-match tests, robustness perturbations and ablations are bounded Validator evidence even though they are neither formal verification nor empirical validation of the ignition architecture. Case studies compose PAW calls with keyword search, regex and deterministic Python in user code, but no learned program-composition algebra, adapter arithmetic or formal router is supplied. The paper supports a versioned distributable artifact concept; current SDKs additionally implement slugs, immutable pinned versions and caches, but those current service features must not be projected backward as a governed paper-era provenance registry. The corrected card therefore remains PARTIAL while superseding the prior card for downstream synthesis.
accepted_prior_claims: PAW defines a hybrid discrete pseudo-program plus continuous PEFT artifact executed by a frozen interpreter.
The main text reports a Qwen3-4B compiler, frozen Qwen3-0.6B interpreter, rank-64 LoRA with 64 shared bases, and FuzzyBench-10M spanning more than 800 task categories.
The paper reports 73.78 exact match for the final 0.6B PAW system versus 68.70 for direct Qwen3-32B prompting, subject to synthetic-benchmark and system-comparability limits.
The compiler/interpreter split and reusable single-file artifact are concrete evidence for Function OS representation, compiler, artifact and interpreter nodes.
The paper provides no formal specification language, semantic-equivalence checker, effect calculus or formal correctness guarantee.

material_corrections.corrected: The paper says the synthetic 10M-example dataset is released; the currently public Hugging Face dataset is ungated but contains only 50,678 verified test/test_clean examples, so full 10M training-corpus availability was not verified.

material_corrections.prior: Correctness is probabilistic and the paper explicitly acknowledges this.
material_corrections.corrected: The paper supplies empirical exact-match, ablation, robustness and runtime evaluations but no probabilistic semantics or explicit probabilistic-correctness claim; current SDKs default to temperature-zero decoding, while paper-level decoding determinism is not established as a semantic guarantee.

Appendix case studies demonstrate external orchestration of multiple calls in user code; they do not define PAW-artifact composition, adapter arithmetic, learned compositional compilation or a formal router.

material_corrections.prior: Direct support for a versioned registry and package-manager distribution.
material_corrections.corrected: The paper directly supports named/versioned, cached and distributable single-file artifacts as a design concept. Current SDK slugs, immutable @vN references, cache policy and hosted lookup are later/current operational evidence, not a governed provenance registry or an immutable paper result.

material_corrections.prior: NO_EVIDENCE because validation is not formal.
material_corrections.corrected: Bounded empirical Validator evidence exists through exact-match benchmarks, controlled ablations, noisy-specification tests, local runtime checks and small deployed case studies; this is not formal verification, architecture proof or empirical validation of Function OS.

specification_language: Unstructured natural-language function descriptions, optionally with examples and constraints, transformed by a pseudo compiler into a restatement-plus-examples token sequence. There is no typed contract, formal pre/postcondition language or machine-checked specification semantics.
uncertainty_model: No calibrated uncertainty, confidence, abstention, repeated-run dispersion or probabilistic semantics is supplied. Main results are predominantly point estimates on synthetic data; the verified subset uses agreement between gpt-5.2 and gpt-5-mini as a label-quality filter, not a PAW uncertainty model. Robustness scores under perturbed specifications are sensitivity evidence only.
lifecycle_and_provenance: The paper presents a reusable single-file artifact that can be named, versioned, cached and distributed, but it does not give an immutable build receipt, dataset manifest, compiler/interpreter compatibility contract, signed provenance, rollback protocol or governed registry schema. Current public Python/JS SDKs add versioned slugs, immutable pinned versions and caching; current compiler and verified-test artifacts are public snapshots, but the compiler model card lacks a declared license and the full 10M training split was not located.
composition_rule: Only external sequential/orchestrated composition in ordinary user code is demonstrated. The 10-function tool-calling pipeline delegates time parsing to regex and JSON assembly to deterministic Python; the reranking case combines a keyword index with a PAW reranker. No algebra over LoRA artifacts, merge safety, associativity, routing contract or learned multi-step composition is validated.
state_or_effect_model: The paper models a per-call autoregressive fuzzy function and does not define persistent state, external effects, effect types, transactional behavior or effect routing. Autoregressive token state within a call must not be conflated with a Function OS state/effect model.
validation_regime: Empirical exact-match evaluation on synthetic FuzzyBench splits, six small image tasks, component ablations, noisy-specification perturbations, a 4,096-example quantization subset, two 36-example compact-model sets and case studies. No formal proof, architecture-level empirical validation, equivalence certificate, independent replication, repeated-run uncertainty or comprehensive external-domain validation is established.
equivalence_notions: Exact string match to synthetic references is the principal task metric. It is not semantic equivalence between specifications, generated artifacts, PEFT methods, compiler versions or a symbolic reference implementation.

source_specific_acceptance_reasoning: The prior review correctly captured the central bounded result: the numerator and normalization state of causal linear attention can be written as an incrementally programmed fast-weight associative memory, and a learned delta-style update provides an explicit state-dependent write instruction. Material corrections are nevertheless required. The exact registered bytes are arXiv v3, not v1. Capacity is bounded by the feature-space dimension d_dot under an orthogonality/interference argument, not generically by the raw matrix dimension; DPFP changes d_dot and the empirical threshold is approximate. There is no standalone compiler or persistent program artifact: slow learned projections produce keys, values and write strengths online inside a layer, W and z are ephemeral recurrent state, and queries read that state. The paper's stochastic training and FAVOR+ random features do not make the fast-weight function semantically probabilistic; DPFP is expressly deterministic. Empirical results support the proposed update relative to matched sum-update linear baselines, but DPFP does not beat the standard Transformer or the largest Performer configuration on WMT14, Delta Net remains worse than the standard Transformer in the limited-context WikiText table, and it trails Transformer-XL with sufficiently larger state in the untruncated comparison. The official synthetic repository supplies source and 320 CSV logs, but the driver effectively uses one fixed seed because the parsed --seed value is not passed to run, reports best validation values without dispersion, and regenerates FAVOR+ Omega on every forward call even in evaluation although the paper says evaluation features are fixed. The separate language-model repository has code but no tracked tests, result logs or checkpoints, and no pinned translation port was found. The corrected record therefore remains PARTIAL and supersedes the prior card for synthesis.
accepted_prior_claims: Causal linear attention admits a concrete fast-weight representation W plus normalization accumulator z, updated by outer products and read by a query.
The delta instruction reads the current value at a key, learns a sigmoid write strength beta and updates W by beta times the value error outer-product the key feature.
The paper gives a bounded orthogonality/interference capacity argument and tests it on synthetic associative retrieval.
DPFP is a deterministic parameter-free feature map intended to increase projected dimension and encourage sparse, more orthogonal keys.
Mutable fast-weight memory is explicit within sequence processing, while no typed effect system, persistent artifact registry or program-equivalence checker is provided.

material_corrections.corrected: The exact frozen hash/size bytes and arXiv API identify arXiv:2102.11174v3; the 16 pages combine the 12-page PMLR paper and 4-page supplement.

material_corrections.prior: Linear self-attention mechanisms are formally equivalent to FWPs.
material_corrections.corrected: The paper rewrites causal linearised attention's core numerator as an outer-product fast-weight memory and includes accumulator z for normalization. This is a mechanism-level algebraic correspondence, not an equivalence of whole Transformers, trained programs or observable semantics.

material_corrections.prior: Capacity is bounded by matrix dimension d.
material_corrections.corrected: The interference argument uses at most d_dot mutually orthogonal key features; d_dot depends on phi and equals 2*d_key*nu for DPFP. It is an idealized upper-bound argument with approximate empirical thresholds, not a universal exact capacity theorem for trained sequence models.

material_corrections.prior: The matrix is overwritten at each step.
material_corrections.corrected: Additive linear attention accumulates outer products. The proposed delta state transition selectively removes and writes the association along the current key; it does not replace the entire matrix.

material_corrections.prior: Self-attention is a concrete compiler and W dot q is a separately executed interpreter.
material_corrections.corrected: This is a useful architectural analogy only: learned slow projections generate online write/read vectors inside one causal layer, not an offline compiler producing a persistent deployable artifact for an independent interpreter.

material_corrections.prior: The FWP learns by gradient descent and its behavior is probabilistic.
material_corrections.corrected: Training is stochastic and FAVOR+ introduces output variance through sampled features, but the paper supplies no probabilistic program semantics. The proposed DPFP path is deterministic given parameters and inputs.

material_corrections.prior: Translation and language-model experiments show competitive or improved performance compared with standard linear attention.
material_corrections.corrected: Delta updates consistently improve matched sum-update linear baselines in reported WikiText settings. DPFP improves small-d_dot linear alternatives on WMT14 but scores 27.1 test versus 27.7 for both the standard Transformer and the largest Performer; Delta Net is 31.5 versus standard Transformer 29.6 in the medium limited-context table and 29.4 versus Transformer-XL 25.5 when the latter uses much larger state.

material_corrections.prior: No Validator evidence because validation is not formal.
material_corrections.corrected: Equation-level identities, synthetic capacity/update tests, WMT/WikiText evaluations and ablations are bounded behavioral-check evidence. They are not an architecture proof, semantic-equivalence service or empirical validation of Function OS; source receipts are incomplete and no independent reproduction was performed.

specification_language: No external function-specification language is defined. The input sequence induces online keys, values, queries and write strengths through trained projections; training objectives rather than contracts specify useful behavior.
uncertainty_model: No calibrated predictive uncertainty, acceptance threshold or repeated-run dispersion is reported. Synthetic figures use the best validation loss per model/size; the released driver defaults effectively to one seed and evaluates 20 sampled sequences. FAVOR+ samples random feature matrices and the paper notes output variance, whereas DPFP is deterministic. These facts do not amount to probabilistic program semantics.
lifecycle_and_provenance: The programmed W and z are per-sequence runtime state, initialized to zero and normally not persisted or versioned. The paper-linked MIT synthetic repository is a ten-commit, untagged snapshot with 320 CSV logs but no tests/checkpoints; its --seed argument is not propagated and its FAVOR+ evaluation implementation does not visibly fix Omega. The Apache language-model repository's current head postdates the paper and contains scripts/source but no tests, results or checkpoints. The described FAIRSEQ translation port is not pinned in the linked assets. No artifact identity, compatibility manifest, signed provenance, migration or rollback contract exists.
composition_rule: Programming instructions compose sequentially as state transitions over W and z. Additive updates sum outer products; delta updates are state-dependent and beta-gated. This is within-layer temporal accumulation/update, not composition of independently specified function artifacts and not a multi-function router.
state_or_effect_model: W and normalization accumulator z are explicit mutable mathematical state. They are reset to zero per sequence in the derivation; the untruncated-language-model experiment carries fast-weight memory across training segments while truncating backpropagation. No external effects, effect typing, transactions, isolation or persistence contract is defined.
validation_regime: Algebraic mechanism derivations; two synthetic associative-retrieval settings; WMT14 BLEU; WikiText-103 perplexity in limited, non-overcapacity and carried-context configurations; normalization/position/state-size ablations; throughput and memory point measurements. Main results lack multi-seed dispersion/significance. Reported failure boundaries include attention-normalization accumulator growth, divergence without sum normalization in some runs, worse-than-standard baselines, FAVOR+ plus delta NaNs in an appendix setting and finite-capacity interference.
equivalence_notions: Equations 8-19 establish a bounded computational correspondence between causal linearised attention and normalized outer-product fast-weight updates. Appendix B compares two update rules under orthogonal-key assumptions and shows preservation of an unrelated association for the proposed rule. Neither result provides behavioral equivalence between trained models, specifications, checkpoints or implementations.

A universal exact capacity law for arbitrary trained Transformers.
Composition or routing of independently specified functions.
Typed contracts, external-effect safety or persistent state lifecycle.
Behavioral equivalence between trained models or implementations.
Probabilistic program semantics, calibrated uncertainty or fuzzy-function semantics.
A claim that DPFP/Delta Net dominates standard Transformers or large-state Transformer-XL across reported tasks.
Multi-seed statistical certainty or a complete immutable reproduction bundle for all tables.
